detail: wrong: the full share is always paid on the turn → the full equity share is paid out on the turn
reason: Equity is a probability-weighted showdown share, not chips paid on the turn; a later fold can forfeit potential wins.

detail: wrong: any two cards that pair the board → pairing the board across the two remaining cards
reason: Pairing board ranks does not ensure the two additional spades needed to reach five spades.

detail: wrong: the preflop raiser should always bet / the last actor always has initiative → the preflop raise obliges the raiser to c-bet / acting last gives a player the initiative
reason: Preflop aggression does not require a c-bet; acting last determines position, not which player has betting initiative.

detail: wrong: when only sets and bluffs use it → when sets and bluffs form the betting range
reason: A range of sets and bluffs is polarized, not the merged strong-and-medium value range asked about; worse made-hand calls justify the small value bet.

detail: wrong: value only → a pure value range
reason: The listed unpaired hands are bluffs alongside sets, so the 8 BB range is not pure value.

detail: wrong: a second size always makes a policy more profitable → adding a second size itself increases profitability
reason: Adding a second size alone does not increase EV if responses and payoffs remain identical.

detail: wrong: only the bet stays in the pot → the bet enters the pot but the call does not
reason: Both the bet and its matched call increase the pot for the next street.

detail: wrong: any low-card flop makes a wide c-bet safe → low flop ranks by themselves make a wide c-bet safe
reason: Low ranks alone do not make broad c-betting safe; connected low boards can favor the caller’s pairs and draws.

detail: wrong: a set should always disguise its strength → having a set is enough reason to hide its strength
reason: A set alone does not justify slowplaying; a passive opponent may check again instead of paying a delayed bet.

detail: wrong: the preflop raiser never has good flush coverage → raising preflop rules out good flush coverage
reason: A preflop raiser can have flushes; legal suited combinations depend on the actual range and board blockers.

detail: wrong: only sets and high-equity semibluffs raise / every raise uses the same amount → the raising range consists of sets and high-equity semibluffs / the raising range uses one size
reason: Sets plus semibluffs describe polarization, not merged raising; using one size does not distinguish merged and polarized ranges.

detail: wrong: raise only top pair because the board has two hearts → reserve raises for top pair because the board has two hearts
reason: The stipulated top pairs call; the polarized raise includes sets and heart-draw bluffs instead.

detail: wrong: every time you act first → when your position lets you act first
reason: Acting first permits a lead but cannot by itself lower showdown cost; opponent calls and raises determine whether the block bet helps.

detail: wrong: every single-spade hand makes a flush → holding one spade is enough to make a flush
reason: Three board spades plus one hole-card spade make four spades, not the five needed for a flush.

detail: wrong: the premium pairs only → the premium pairs rather than the caller’s group
reason: Each listed suited caller class supplies the two missing straight ranks; premium pocket pairs cannot supply two distinct ranks here.

detail: wrong: only when a 4-bet matches the 3-bet → when the 4-bet matches the 3-bet rather than increasing it
reason: Matching a 3-bet is a call, not a 4-bet, which must increase the wager.

detail: wrong: every checked 3-bet flop signals a trap → a checked flop in a 3-bet pot signals a trap
reason: A check in a 3-bet pot alone cannot establish a trap or justify checking back; weak and marginal hands can check too.

detail: wrong: a three-way pot can never be value-bet → a third player prevents value betting
reason: A third player does not prevent value betting; multiple worse ranges may still pay a strong hand.

detail: wrong: every call is a bluff → the callers have bluff holdings rather than made hands
reason: The stated continuing groups contain sets and top pairs, not bluff holdings.

detail: wrong: only the first player can pay → the first player can pay, but the second cannot
reason: Both modeled players have worse made hands that can call the river bet, including after the first calls.

detail: wrong: always the opening raiser / always the first player to check → the opening raiser / the first player to check
reason: Neither being the opener nor checking first guarantees last action; a live player behind can still bet.

detail: wrong: only co → co rather than btn or bb
reason: The stated CO overpairs cannot supply both T and 9; BTN and BB can each hold T9s for the nut straight.

detail: wrong: it closes all action because the blind checked → it ends the betting round because the blind checked
reason: BTN remains live and has not acted, so CO’s check after BB does not close the betting round.

detail: wrong: every hand in bb’s full range is a straight → bb’s full range consists of straights
reason: The listed straight classes demonstrate a subset of BB’s range, not that its full range contains only straights.

detail: wrong: every pot if its hand is best / only its own chips back → the main and side pots if its hand is best / its own contribution, without the matched chips
reason: A short stack cannot win the side pot it did not match, but can win opponents’ matched contributions in the eligible main pot.

detail: wrong: 60.5 bb all in the main pot → 60.5 bb in a single main pot
reason: The 8 BB starting pot plus three 7.5 BB matches gives 30.5 BB main; the two extra 10 BB contributions give 20 BB side, not a single 60.5 BB main.

detail: wrong: yes, because any extra amount reopens → yes, because increasing the wager is enough to reopen
reason: The increase from 6 to 9 BB is only 3 BB, below the stated 6 BB full-raise threshold for reopening.

detail: wrong: no. all-in wagers never reopen → no. an all-in wager cannot reopen betting
reason: An all-in can be a full raise; the increase from 5 to 11 BB is 6 BB and reopens action under the stated rule.

detail: wrong: the equilibrium maximizes profit against every actual opponent → the equilibrium is the profit-maximizing response to an opponent’s actual strategy
reason: An equilibrium prevents profitable unilateral deviations against its equilibrium counterpart, but a different opponent may permit a more profitable best response.

detail: wrong: assume the quick bet is always a bluff / assume that opponent uses every equilibrium frequency → classify the quick bet as a bluff from its speed / treat the opponent’s strategy as matching the equilibrium frequencies
reason: A single quick bet does not establish bluff frequency, and using an equilibrium baseline does not establish that an unknown opponent follows it.

detail: wrong: to every street for players on that site / to every individual at that stake → across the streets played on that site / to individual players at that stake as their personal tendency
reason: Pool tendencies are specific to comparable decision nodes, and neither other streets nor individual players necessarily share the measured average.

detail: wrong: all preflop hands that the regular played → the regular’s complete preflop hand sample
reason: The full preflop sample includes hands that never reach the relevant river decision, so it is not the appropriate denominator.

detail: wrong: change all preflop opening charts → revise the preflop opening strategy across positions
reason: A read about calls in a specific postflop node does not establish a reason to revise preflop opening ranges.

detail: wrong: no evidence of any kind → anonymity makes the available evidence unusable
reason: Anonymity limits player-specific histories but leaves observable evidence about format, action line, size and stack depth.

detail: wrong: a pure action is unexploitable against every response → a pure action is protected against changes in the opponent’s response
reason: A pure action tied against one fixed strategy need not remain equally profitable against a changed opponent response.

detail: wrong: any amount of checking occurred → the opponent checked at some point in the hand
reason: Checking does not establish a range cap because strong hands may check and weaker hands can improve later.

detail: wrong: co holding any missed hands → co having missed hands in the retained range
reason: The retained full houses disprove a cap below them but do not exclude missed hands that the model explicitly retains.

detail: wrong: all hands dealt in the session / only the hands you called and lost → the total number of hands dealt in the session / the number of losing calls
reason: Session-wide hands include irrelevant decisions, while losing calls omit folds and winning calls, so neither denominator measures defense at the target node.

detail: wrong: call all marginal pairs until the count reaches mdf → use marginal-pair calls to raise defense to mdf
reason: Against the observed value-heavy range, meeting MDF alone does not make marginal-pair calls profitable.

detail: wrong: the river bet is almost always a bluff → the river betting range is overwhelmingly bluffs
reason: One elapsed time is insufficient to infer that the river betting range is predominantly bluffs.

detail: wrong: ignore every live behavior forever → exclude live behavior from your long-term reads
reason: Discarding live behavior categorically misses repeated comparable observations that can support a meaningful read.

detail: wrong: the player plays at the same time every day → the player keeps a consistent daily playing schedule
reason: A consistent playing schedule may identify a regular but does not show a high calling frequency at a specific node.

detail: wrong: every large river bluff now wins → large river bluffs now win through the player’s risk aversion
reason: One fold and a remark about stakes suggest a hypothesis but establish neither risk aversion as the cause nor a profitable bluff frequency.

detail: wrong: all players behind call every raise size → players behind respond to raises by calling at each size
reason: Players calling raises at each size undermine isolation rather than supporting a raise to play heads-up.

detail: wrong: only the limper you target / only the larger blind → the targeted limper, excluding players outside that match-up / bb, with hj and sb excluded
reason: Ignoring the other limper or either blind misses live players whose calls could prevent a heads-up pot.

detail: wrong: it permanently makes every future value bet profitable → the shown bluff secures lasting profitability for future value bets
reason: Showing a bluff may change an opponent’s calls but does not guarantee lasting value-bet profitability across opponents and sizes.

detail: wrong: reset your entire read on every player at the table → rebuild your reads for the whole table from this regular’s calls
reason: The regular’s observed calls support a specific adjustment against that player rather than a reset of every table read.

detail: wrong: only the two hands you remember / discard all seven because the player surprised you → the two bluffs from your memory, without the other notes / discard the seven notes because the player surprised you
reason: Keeping only the two memorable bluffs biases the sample, while discarding all seven notes loses the matched evidence.

detail: wrong: continue automatically because the result is positive → keep playing based on the positive result
reason: A positive result does not override the prewritten stop condition once both the profit marker and the specified process failures occur.

detail: wrong: give up all misses because your defense is too wide → remove missed hands from the bluff range because your defense is too wide
reason: Fifteen folds in twenty opportunities show overfolding rather than excessive defense, making additional opponent bluffs profitable here.

detail: wrong: all pots you lost → a record of the session’s lost pots
reason: Selecting lost pots by outcome can omit flawed river value decisions in pots that were won.

detail: wrong: skip the ledger and reconstruct from your result only → reconstruct the call from your result instead of the ledger
reason: The outcome alone cannot reconstruct the action and contribution amounts needed to evaluate the call price.

detail: wrong: book a win every short session / never meet a stronger opponent → finish each short session with a profit / arrange to face opponents no stronger than you
reason: Short-session profit is subject to variance and available opponents cannot be fully controlled, so neither is a reliable actionable goal.

detail: wrong: i will win back any lost profit before taking a break → recover the lost profit before taking a break
reason: Tying a break to recovering lost profit can prolong play despite the decision-process leak the rule is intended to address.

detail: wrong: a only / b only → a with 100% weight / b with 100% weight
reason: Pure A lets the minimizing player choose the second column for a row payoff of −1, while pure B lets that player choose the first column for the same payoff.

detail: wrong: you always bet against 60% of the opponent’s holdings → bet against 60% of the opponent’s holdings using a pure betting strategy
reason: A 60% action frequency describes how often the given hand bets at the node, not a pure bet against 60% of hidden opponent holdings.

detail: wrong: always bet every king-high flop / never check this hand → use a pure betting strategy across king-high flops / remove check from this hand’s strategy
reason: One queried node cannot justify pure betting across king-high flops or eliminating a check that ties the bet in that model.

detail: wrong: replace every opponent action at every street → replace the opponent’s complete strategy across streets
reason: The observed response supports changing the matched river node, not replacing unrelated opponent strategies across streets.

detail: wrong: only how often you wish the opponent would fold / a commitment to bet every later street → a desired fold frequency, without the follow-up branches / commit to betting the turn and river in advance
reason: A flop betting plan must account for called and raised branches and adapt to later cards rather than rely on desired folds or predetermined barrels.

detail: wrong: apply an equilibrium label to any strategy produced → treat the solver’s output as an equilibrium by virtue of its source
reason: A solver output is conditional on its entered action tree, so omitted relevant raises and legal sizes must be evaluated before claiming a best response.

detail: wrong: a decision to call every raise because you have top pair / only a play for the one river you most want → commit top pair to calling raises based on its rank / plan for the desired river card and leave the others unplanned
reason: Top pair must compare call price and equity against possible flushes, while the plan must account for other legal river cards as well as the desired one.

detail: wrong: river · keep all four queens available → river · keep four queens available
reason: All four queens are unseen; excluding Ks and Kh leaves 8 KQ combos, so this note is not the mistake.

reason: 7s completes every modeled opponent straight; reference 2c 79.55% → 1.14%, call → fold.

reason: Both blanks 79.55% = reference; both preserve call and neither is the requested fold turn.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / good for your showdown share → 4c / 3c
reason: Both 81.82% = reference; both preserve call, not the requested fold.

reason: All opponent hands have four jacks; reference 3c and both offered cards give 0%, so no profitable call exists.

detail: wrong: good for your showdown share / bad for your showdown share → 2d / qc
reason: 2d and Qc each leave 0% versus quads; neither makes calling profitable.

reason: Qh completes ace-high flush versus sets; reference 2c 15.91% → 77.27%, fold → call.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / bad for your showdown share → 4c / 7c
reason: Both leave draw uncompleted, 15.91%; neither changes reference fold into call.

reason: 3h gives each set a full house despite Hero's flush; Qh 77.27% → 0%, call → fold.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / good for your showdown share → 2h / 4h
reason: Each makes the same flush versus sets, 77.27% = reference; both remain calls.

reason: Ah pairs every opponent ace, overtaking QQ; 2c 88.64% → 4.55%, call → fold.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / good for your showdown share → 7c / 4c
reason: 7c 85.61% and 4c 88.64% remain above 33⅓%; neither changes the call.

reason: 5s makes full house which modeled draws cannot beat; 2h 22.73% → 100%, fold → call.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / bad for your showdown share → 6h / 3h
reason: Both complete opponents' flushes; 22.73% = reference, so both remain folds.

detail: correct: good for your showdown share → 9h
reason: 9h makes Hero's flush and removes Ah9h from the range; As 25.00% → 84.09%, fold → call.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / bad for your showdown share → ad / ac
reason: Ad and Ac both leave 25.00% against the legal range, so both remain folds.

detail: correct: good for your showdown share → td
reason: Td completes Hero's 6–T straight, giving 96.97% versus 2d 18.18%; fold → call.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / bad for your showdown share → 4c / 3c
reason: Neither completes the straight; each leaves 18.18%, so folds remain correct.

detail: correct: good for your showdown share → 5c
reason: 5c makes a set that stays ahead on every modeled river; 2c 4.55% → 100%, fold → call.

detail: wrong: unchanged showdown share / bad for your showdown share → 4c / 3c
reason: Both improve share to 13.64% (including straight outs) but it is still below 33⅓%; neither is the requested call turn.

detail: wrong: the betting group consists only of one-pair hands / the callers have only made straights → the betting group is a one-pair range / the callers have a made-straight range
reason: The betting group still includes sets and two unpaired classes and the Q-x callers pair the queen without a straight, so both options stay wrong.

detail: wrong: all of the third combo → the third combo at full weight
reason: Three full-weight bluff combos exceed the required 18/7, so full weight on the third combo stays wrong.

detail: wrong: a card removing only the opponent’s folding misses / any ace on any board → a card removing folding misses while leaving the calling range intact / an ace chosen by rank rather than board texture
reason: Removing folding misses leaves fewer hands that release, and an ace helps only when its removal matters on this line, so both options stay wrong.

detail: wrong: any player has matched the big blind voluntarily → a player has matched the big blind voluntarily
reason: A voluntary match of the big blind is a limp, which removes the unopened condition, so the option stays wrong; only the absolute qualifier was dropped.

detail: wrong: a slow river bet always has strong value / a flop snap-call proves a later bluff → a slow river bet signals a strong value range / an immediate flop call proves a later bluff
reason: Unmatched immediate flop calls and a slow river bet cannot establish either a value-heavy river range or a later bluff.

detail: correct: treat risk aversion as a hypothesis and keep the existing priced baseline → treat risk aversion as a hypothesis and keep the decision based on the current range and price
reason: One observed fold does not establish the player’s river fold frequency, so retaining the current range and price while testing the hypothesis is sound.

detail: wrong: limp behind → call 1 bb
reason: Calling the 1 BB limp does not isolate CO, while the 6 BB raise isolates CO in seven of ten paths versus three for 4 BB.

detail: correct: five → 5
reason: The check, direct fold and call, and two responses to a raise total five terminal paths.

detail: wrong: four / six → 4 / 6
reason: Four omits a terminal path and six counts the intermediate raise as a leaf, so both remain incorrect.

detail: correct: a candidate heuristic to test on a matching board family → a possible rule of thumb to test on similar boards
reason: A tie at a single modeled node supports a possible rule to test, not a strategy for untested boards.

detail: correct: use the simplification in the first two nodes with an exception for the third → 2 nodes: use it in the first two, with an exception for the third
reason: The first two costs of 0.02 and 0.04 BB meet the 0.10 BB ceiling, with the 0.28 BB node requiring an exception.

detail: wrong: use it everywhere because two of the three pass / reject it in the first two as well → 3 nodes: use it throughout because two pass / 0 nodes: reject it in the first two as well
reason: Accepting all three includes a node above tolerance, and rejecting all three discards two nodes below tolerance.

detail: wrong: use the baseline output without changing the opponent model → use the original output without changing the opponent model
reason: The original balanced-defense model cannot answer the payoff question against the observed overfold unless that response is changed.

detail: correct: check plan → check plan: 1.5 bb average
reason: The check plan returns (3+2+0+1)/4 = 1.5 BB on average, exceeding the bet plan’s −0.125 BB.

detail: wrong: bet plan because its best outcome is higher / both plans tie because their second branch matches → bet plan because its 5.5 bb peak is higher / both plans tie because branch two returns 2 bb
reason: A 5.5 BB peak or one shared 2 BB outcome cannot outweigh the remaining branches, so neither claim beats the check plan’s average.
